minutes.headline: Conservation Commission held a public forum on firearm hunting in its draft land use policy and took no vote on it.
minutes.summary: The commission spent about an hour at a public forum on revisions to its land use policy, mostly whether to allow firearm hunting on conservation land. The town attorney's comments arrived just before the meeting, so no action was taken and the topic returns at the next meeting. The commission then continued several wetland hearings to December 16 and issued negative determinations on three requests (oak ridge shed, sunset lane dock, 1168 rear Mass Ave demolition) plus a solar tree-removal request, a certificate of compliance and an administrative tree approval.

A select board member urges the commission to keep the firearm restriction; discusses town attorney's opinion and liability.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission held a public forum on firearm hunting in its draft land use policy and took no action; the topic returns at the next meeting.
Commissioners favoring firearm hunting on conservation land were asked to bring concrete drafts to the next meeting.
Several wetland hearings without DEP file numbers, including Page Street lots 1 and 2, were continued to December 16 by roll call.
Negative determinations passed on four requests: 28 Oak Ridge Road, 398 Sunset Lane dock, 1168 Rear Mass Ave demolition and 60 South Row Road solar tree removal.
A certificate of compliance for 137 Bird Street was issued and an administrative tree removal at 106 Sandy Cove Road was approved.

why_it_matters: Whether firearm hunting is allowed on town conservation land is still undecided, so residents who live near or use these parcels can still weigh in before the policy is settled.
Negative determinations mean those projects can go ahead without a full wetlands filing, while continued hearings leave the other projects pending until at least December 16.
watch_next: December 16: continued hearings for Boivin, Page Street lots 1 and 2, 232 Bird Street, 1672 Mass Ave and 25 Pearl.
Next meeting: longer land use policy discussion on firearm hunting and forest harvesting proposals; the first January meeting may be cancelled.
